## Chosen hook

Calm plain opener, feeling-first rather than punchy, per the Facebook format:

"If you are over 40 and putting a slower recovery down to age, there is one cheap number worth ruling out first."

## Script

**Funnel:** TOFU (Attract) | job: problem-aware explainer for the older segment (vitamin D vs ageing) | cta: quiz | format: facebook-post | marker: vitamin-d
**Emotion:** Recognition, then curiosity. Nothing here asks him to feel worried.
**Source:** `14-signs-of-vitamin-d-deficiency` (Pillar A spoke, published 2026-06-19, Ewa-signed).

POST

> If you are over 40 and putting a slower recovery down to age, there is one cheap number worth ruling out first.
>
> The ageing story is convenient because it fits so well. A session you used to shake off in a day now takes two. Stairs feel heavier than they should. There is a dull ache in the shins or the lower back that you cannot pin on any particular session. Every one of those sits on the low vitamin D list, and every one of them is also just what getting older feels like. By feel alone, they are the same thing.
>
> So the honest position is this. One sign on its own means very little. Three or four clustering together is worth checking. And no list, including that one, replaces a blood test.
>
> The part most men miss is not on the symptom list at all. Low vitamin D can run quiet for years, so by the time the signs are unmistakable you have usually been low for a long time. The most reliable indicator in this country is not a symptom, it is the calendar. From October to March, UK sunlight is too weak for skin to make meaningful vitamin D, and most UK men sit in the insufficient band between January and April without ever knowing it.
>
> Which makes late summer an unusually useful moment to look. The swing between summer and winter is bigger than most men realise, and a reading now tells you which end of that swing you are starting the dark half of the year from.
>
> Vitamin D contributes to normal muscle function. Recovery is one of the first places men say they notice something has shifted in the dark months.
>
> One line worth knowing before you test anything: a reading under 25 nmol/L is a GP conversation rather than a wellness one.
>
> If you are not sure which check makes sense for what you are actually feeling, this walks you through it in a couple of minutes: https://andro-prime.com/test-selector?utm_source=facebook

## Craft notes

- **Archetype:** Teacher, which `written-post-playbook.md` names as one of the three Facebook homes. The older Facebook reader is patient and clinical-curious, so the post is built to be worth reading even if nobody clicks, which is the format's stated job.
- **Structure chosen on avatar fit, and that is the axis it was ranked on.** The obvious Facebook shape for this hub is the countdown of the fourteen signs. It was rejected: a list is exactly what this reader has already read, and the hub's own fourteenth entry is the argument that the list cannot answer his question. Running the list would reproduce the problem the source article exists to correct. The chosen shape uses three signs as recognition and then turns to the thing no symptom can tell him. Both clear compliance identically, so avatar fit was the only live axis.
- **Seasonally honest rather than seasonally opportunistic.** Published in August, the post does not pretend winter is here. It says a late-summer reading tells you where you start the dark half from, which is what the hub's summer-to-winter swing actually supports. A winter-scarcity framing in August would have been the stronger hook and a worse claim.
- **The one EFSA claim is quoted exactly, and it stands on its own sentence for a reason.** The approved wording appears in `03_compliance/CONTEXT.md` and in the hub verbatim. The first draft of this post welded it to the recovery observation with "which is part of why", which asserted a causal link the hub does not: the hub states the approved claim, then separately reports what men say they notice. Pre-flight caught it and the two are now two sentences, as they are in the source. Worth recording because a compression that reads as tightening is the commonest way a derivative quietly exceeds its canonical asset.
- **The GP line is carried, not dropped.** Under 25 nmol/L goes to a GP in the body, in the hub's own terms.
- **No personal history, no bloodwork figure, and nothing written as Mark.** The only figures are the NICE band and the NICE deficiency threshold, both quoted from the hub.
- **`cta: quiz` matches both the queue row and the Facebook format**, which routes to the router rather than to the article. The link carries the full `https://` scheme. Note that `written-post-playbook.md` records the scheme rule as ruled for LinkedIn and explicitly **not yet ruled for Facebook**; the full scheme is used here as the safer default, and it is flagged below rather than recorded as settled.
- **No thumbnail is owed, ruled by Keith 2026-08-05.** A Facebook post does not need a bespoke cover; Facebook Reels and videos do. Imagery for a post comes from the associated blog article's own photo, used as published rather than re-treated. This rendition is `thumb: none` and the image attached at scheduling is the vitamin D article's own `imgSrc`.

## Rails held

Written as an allowlist of what the copy does, never a list of what it avoids (Observation 83).

The post stays on the education side throughout. It names three body-feel cues, says plainly that they are indistinguishable from ageing by feel alone, and states that a list cannot answer the question a reading can. It carries one EFSA-approved ingredient claim in its exact approved wording and attaches it to no outcome. The two figures are the NICE insufficient band and the NICE deficiency threshold, both quoted from the spoke; no personal result appears. The deficiency case is routed to a GP in the body. The marker is vitamin D, which is live in Kit 2, satisfying the live-marker rail. The single CTA is a soft in-post link to the test selector, which the funnel map allows at TOFU, so nothing here points at a kit or at the founding-member list. Native upload applies to any image used. No em dashes, no bullet lists in the post body, no engagement bait.
